newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes creep higher in end-of-month demand.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes creep higher in end-of-month demand.

text.p: Crude oil prices in Asia crept higher on Thursday as end-of-month demand chased dwindling availabilities, traders said.
Brent/Dubai and Dubai intermonth paper levels were steady, although paper Tapis edged up in line with overnight crude numbers.
January Tapis was valued at $24.65/$24.80, up 20 cents.

Minas crude -- which traders say is the only Indonesian grade left available for January -- edged up above ICP +80 cents again after most assessments through the week had been placed at ICP +75 cents.
Traders reported a Murban deal at ADNOC +73 cents, Umm Shaif at +79 cents -- a package deal to a U.S. major and Lower Zakum at 76 cents.

However, some sellers said they saw good demand still and would stand off the market to wait for bids to rise. One major said he still had Murban, Lower Zakum and Umm Shaif available and would wait for bids to hit the 80s before selling.
Further demand is to come from the Bangchak and Indian tenders, which close later on Thursday. Bangchak is expected to award on Friday and India over the weekend.
Traders said a Japanese trader sold 150,000 barrels of Minas into China, which has been the main driving force behind the firm Indonesia crude this month.
Another deal was heard done at above ICP +80 from another Japanese trader into China.

Small parcels of Oman crude maintained a firm edge for Middle East grades for February. A French major sold 200,000 barrels to a Japanese trader at MPM +30 cents and a U.S. major was heard selling a similar amount at MPM +35 cents.
Other Middle East grades traded in line with recent premium levels.
